objective: Offline test harness for RescueStock: net guard, node-proc, server-proc, app-harness, fixtures and playwright helpers, the p95/suite-time report, the start and old-Node tests, the package scan, the health/config contract test and the clean-checkout script (phase b-foundation, last task).
context: Built against spec revision 3 (Testing Strategy: Layout, Commands, Integration start-health and start-old-node, Timing; Deployment: Node floor, ARCH-24) and brief NFR1/NFR5. Depends on b1 (src/app.js, src/index.js, src/main.js, config, routes health/config, scripts/check-node.cjs, scripts/seed.js), b2 (fixture file) and b4 (.env.example, README). package.json (b1) was not edited; its scripts already call the files built here (pretest reset-test-out.js, test --import net-guard.js, posttest report-p95.js).
expectedOutput: test/helpers/{net-guard,node-proc,server-proc,app-harness,fixtures,playwright}.js; scripts/{report-p95,reset-test-out}.js and clean-checkout.sh; start-health, start-old-node, package scan, health-config and net-guard self-tests; npm test passing offline with the guard.
acceptanceCriteria: net-guard.js patches net.connect, net.Socket.prototype.connect, tls.connect, dns.lookup and globalThis.fetch; any non-loopback host throws NETWORK_BLOCKED and fails the test (self-test included)

node-proc.js passes the allow-listed execArgv and merges --experimental-sqlite --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning into NODE_OPTIONS (keeping an existing value) when Node < 22.13 (ARCH-24); server-proc.js starts src/index.js with PORT=0, a temp RS_DB_PATH, fake adapters, RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, RS_TEST_HOOKS=1 and reads the listening port from stdout; app-harness.js runs createApp in-process with a fixed clock and records request latency to test/.out/latency.jsonl

NFR1: test/scan/package.test.js checks dependencies, devDependencies, engines and the check-node prefix of every flagged script; start-old-node.test.js runs the exact start string through /bin/sh -c with /opt/node20/bin and /opt/node21/bin (or RS_OLD_NODE_BINS) first on PATH and asserts exit != 0 and stderr matching 'needs Node >= 22.13 (found'; start-health.test.js spawns the start equivalent and gets /api/health 200

scripts/clean-checkout.sh copies the project's git-tracked and unignored files (excluding .eccode/) into an empty temp directory, runs npm install, npm test and npm start there, and asserts GET /api/health 200; it uses only variable names, never secrets
scripts/report-p95.js reads test/.out/latency.jsonl, fails at p95 >= 300 ms and at a suite time >= 5 min from the pretest timestamp
npm test passes offline with the net guard, launches no browser, and its output names each test with its criterion id
completedWork: net-guard.js patches net.connect/createConnection, Socket.prototype.connect, tls.connect, dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup and fetch (strings, URLs, Requests); loopback = localhost names, 127/8, ::1, ::ffff:127.x; unix paths and existing sockets pass. A blocked call throws NETWORK_BLOCKED at the call site, is recorded, and a process that exits 0 with an untaken record is forced to exit 1, so a swallowed attempt still fails the test file (takeBlocked() acknowledges deliberate blocks; setQuiet silences stderr for the self-test). Observed: node --test children inherit '--import ./test/helpers/net-guard.js' and also '--test-concurrency=4', so node-proc.js keeps only --experimental-sqlite, --disable-warning=* and the net-guard import (normalised to an absolute path), always adds the guard, drops NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, and merges the sqlite flags into NODE_OPTIONS (existing value kept, no duplicates) when the version is < 22.13. server-proc.js (startServer) runs src/index.js through node-proc with PORT=0, HOST=127.0.0.1, temp RS_DB_PATH/RS_UPLOAD_DIR, RS_PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake, RS_MODEL_PROVIDER=fake, RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, RS_TEST_HOOKS=1, RS_DEMO_DATE, RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY=1000, RS_MAX_LIVE_RESERVATIONS_PER_CUSTOMER=1; it clears inherited RS_*/PORT/HOST/ANTHROPIC_* names, reads the port from the listening JSON line, exposes request/stop/kill/cleanup, and reports an early exit with stderr instead of hanging. app-harness.js runs createApp in-process (fixed clock 2026-10-20 09:00 Amman, temp SQLite, fake adapters, optional RS-FIX-1 seed with a test-only demo password) and appends one JSON line per request to test/.out/latency.jsonl. fixtures.js: RS-FIX-1 loader, demo users, a cookie/CSRF client with signIn/register/signOut per the Authentication contract. playwright.js: resolvePlaywright (local @playwright/test, then global via RS_GLOBAL_NODE_MODULES, NODE_PATH, <node prefix>/lib/node_modules) and a launchChromium that npm test never calls. scripts/reset-test-out.js empties test/.out and writes suite-start.json; scripts/report-p95.js computes nearest-rank p95, fails at >= 300 ms, at >= 300 s since the pretest timestamp, and on missing/empty/malformed data. test/scan/package.test.js (rules as functions, also run against broken objects), start-old-node.test.js (runs the exact start and seed strings under /bin/sh -c on the real Node 20.20.0 and 21.7.3, asserts exit != 0, the floor message with the found version, empty stdout; skips with a reason when no older Node exists), start-health.test.js (gate, then src/index.js with the flags parsed from the start script; 200 {status:ok}, requestId equals X-Request-Id, 421 for a foreign Host, SIGTERM exits 0), test/api/health-config.test.js (200 shapes, requestId rules, 405, 421, 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After 1 on a closed database, /api/config key set and types, sentinel-value and key-name scans for secrets, client ids and merchant ids under a Sandbox configuration). Unit tests for every helper under test/unit/helpers. scripts/clean-checkout.sh copies tracked plus unignored files (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, minus .eccode/, node_modules, data, test/.out) into mktemp, runs npm install (registry reachable here: 'added 3 packages'), npm test, and npm start with PORT=0 reading the port from the listening line, asserts GET /api/health = '200 ok', stops the process group, removes the temp dir; it unsets RS_*/PORT/HOST/key variables by name and prints no environment. Results: npm test 364 tests, 364 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; p95 15.1 ms over 18 recorded requests; suite 14.7 s; clean-checkout exit 0.
remainingIssues: Criterion ids in test names: every test written in this task is named with its id (NFR1, NFR3, NFR4, NFR5, NFR6, RS-34), but about 113 of the 367 ok lines in the npm test output come from b1/b2 files and carry no criterion id (for example test/unit/db/*.test.js, parts of test/unit/config/*.test.js, test/unit/domain/*). The sixth acceptance criterion is therefore met for b3's tests, not for the whole suite; renaming those tests is outside b3's file ownership. The phase review should route it to b1/b2, and a later scan test could enforce the prefix once they are renamed.

The failing-state run (ev:ev-mv1gppzk-014ca419) was recorded after the net guard, node-proc, server-proc, app-harness, fixtures, playwright and report/reset scripts already existed; it fails on the six files that did not exist yet (start-health, start-old-node, package scan, health-config, clean-checkout.sh), not on an empty tree.

The Node 22.5-22.12 branch of node-proc (NODE_OPTIONS merge) is verified by simulating the version (unit tests, plus a real child started with version 22.12.0 that receives the merged NODE_OPTIONS next to an existing value); no real Node 22.5-22.12 exists on this host. start-old-node ran against real Node 20.20.0 and 21.7.3.

start-health.test.js mirrors the start script (gate, then node <flags> src/index.js with PORT=0) rather than running 'npm start' on a fixed port; the literal 'npm start' is exercised only by scripts/clean-checkout.sh.

scripts/clean-checkout.sh does not run 'npm run seed' (a README step): the seed prints generated demo credentials to the terminal and the criterion lists only install, test and start. It needs git, npm, node and the npm registry; if the registry is unreachable it stops with 'npm install failed' instead of skipping the step.

Latency samples exist only for requests made through app-harness.request (18 now, from health-config and the harness unit tests, which use the default recording). Later API test files must use the harness client for NFR5's p95 to cover them; report-p95.js fails when there are no samples.

fixtures.js signIn/register follow the Authentication contract (GET /api/auth/csrf, POST /api/auth/signin|register with X-CSRF-Token, cookie rs_sid) and are tested against a scripted stand-in only; the auth routes (task c1) do not exist yet, so the first c1 API test must confirm the helper against the real routes.
The spec layout also lists test/helpers/paypal-stub.js and webhook-signer.js; they are not in b3's outputs and belong with the payments tasks.
A deliberate network block in a future test must call takeBlocked() (see test/unit/helpers/net-guard.test.js); otherwise the guard fails the test file at exit, by design.

No defect found in package.json: the scripts pretest/test/posttest that npm test needs are present and correct, so none is routed to the phase review. No defect found in b1/b2/b4 code during this task; /api/health and /api/config, the 405/421/503 paths, check-node.cjs and .env.example behaved as specified.
nextAction: delivery-lead: dispatch the independent phase review for b-foundation (b1, b2, b3, b4); route the missing criterion ids in b1/b2 test names to their owners; backend-engineer (c1) to run the first API test with createClient().signIn against the real auth routes.

lessonDecisions.note: Applies-when condition not met: this task builds test helpers and scripts, not a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project record. The only related point, taking the project root from the script's own location instead of the outer repository, is built into scripts/clean-checkout.sh and exercised by the passing clean-checkout run.
